whyItems.title: Focused tools
whyItems.body: Each app does one job, like planning a date, settling shared expenses, keeping memories, without burying it in menus.

whyItems.title: Pick what fits
whyItems.body: Every couple is different. Install only the apps that match your relationship, skip the rest.

whyItems.title: Better together
whyItems.body: The apps share one design language and one account-free philosophy, so they feel like a family.

whyItems.title: Always growing
whyItems.body: New apps ship regularly. The library grows with your relationship.

faqItems.q: Is TheCoupleApp one app or several?
faqItems.a: One so far. TheCoupleApp is a growing library of small, focused apps for couples. HourStory is the first release, and more will ship as they're genuinely ready. You'll only ever need to install the ones that fit your relationship.

faqItems.q: How much do the apps cost?
faqItems.a: Every app is free to download. Some add an optional paid upgrade, and HourStory, for example, has an optional premium plan.

faqItems.q: Which devices do the apps run on?
faqItems.a: The apps are built for iOS and Android, and are listed on the App Store and Google Play as they launch.

faqItems.q: Do both partners need to install the app?
faqItems.a: Yes, since HourStory, like every app in the library, is built for two. Each partner captures on their own device, and you both watch the day unfold together.

faqItems.q: What languages is this site available in?
faqItems.a: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Hindi and Arabic. Use the language switcher in the footer to change it.

about.title: About TheCoupleApp
body: TheCoupleApp is an umbrella brand for a growing library of apps for couples. Instead of one app that tries to do everything, we ship many small ones, each solving one specific problem really well.
Communication, planning, memories, finances, wellness, fun: every area of a relationship deserves a tool that is simple enough to actually get used.
storyBody: TheCoupleApp started with a small, specific want: one simple tool for one part of a relationship. What we found instead were apps that wanted to be everything at once, like a planner, a journal, a budget, a conversation starter, a mood tracker, with the thing we had actually come for buried a few menus deep.

There is no shortage of apps for couples. What we could not find was a set of small ones. Every product seemed to grow in the same direction: more features, more tabs, more reasons to open it and stay a while. The more they added, the less any single part of them got used.

So we started shipping the opposite. One app per problem, small enough to understand in a minute and finish in two. HourStory came first, for the ache of being apart during the day, when by evening the small things have already faded. The rest of the library is being built the same way, one focused app at a time, released when it is genuinely ready.
whoWeAreBody: TheCoupleApp is an independent project, not a venture-backed company or a large team. It exists because most relationship apps try to do everything at once and end up doing none of it well.
The whole library is built around one idea: an app should be opened, used for a couple of minutes, and closed. No feeds, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase.
whatWeDoBody: We design and publish small apps for couples, one problem at a time, like communication, planning, memories, finances, wellness and fun. Each app ships with its own focused feature set instead of becoming a menu inside one large product.
Every app is free to download on iOS and Android, and some offer an optional paid upgrade. New apps join the library as they are ready.

editorial.title: Editorial guidelines
editorial.description: How the app descriptions, feature lists and FAQs on TheCoupleApp are written, translated and corrected.
editorial.intro: These guidelines cover the written content on this site: app descriptions, feature lists, frequently asked questions, blog posts, and the translations of all of it. This site does not publish news coverage of other companies, reviews of other companies' products, or sponsored articles, since blog posts here are about our own apps and the decisions behind them.

sections.heading: Who writes this content
body: Everything here is written and maintained by the person who builds the apps. There is no separate editorial team, and no content is contributed by advertisers or other third parties.

sections.heading: Accuracy
body: App descriptions describe what an app does today, not what it is planned to do. Apps that have not shipped are labelled as coming soon and are never presented as available.

Details that change, like price, platforms, store availability, live in a single catalog that every page is generated from, so a correction is made in one place and takes effect everywhere it appears.

sections.heading: What is not published here
body: No testimonials, ratings, review counts, awards or endorsements appear unless they are real and can be substantiated. Where there are none, none are shown rather than inventing them.
No paid placement. The only apps listed are our own, and no one can pay to appear in the library or to be described more favourably.

sections.heading: Translations
body: English is the source language. Other languages are translated to carry the same meaning rather than word for word, and product names are left untranslated.
If a translation is missing for any piece of text, the English original is shown in its place rather than an empty space.
